did: Tin Bird, the agent's character in the conversation essays, now has its own animated loop for each of its nine emotions: neutral, curious, taciturn, happy, perplexed, anxious, frustrated, angry and ceremonious. Each one changes the bird's silhouette (wings out, hopping, tilting, bowing) and adds a small sign of the feeling (sweat, steam, sparks, a question mark, dots for a silence), so it reads in a long shot as well as a close-up. The bird gained wings, lids and an opening beak, tucked away so its still picture is unchanged. When a scene gives it a point to look at, it points there with the near wing. A loop starts with its beat and carries on through beats that only move the bird. A contact sheet shows every emotion at three moments and three shot sizes, live.

calls.title: How Tin Bird points (C1525)
options: Point the near wing at the beat's point to look at, whatever the emotion
Add a separate point-at choice to each beat
Leave pointing out until a pose choice exists
calls.why: The beat already carries one point; a new field would widen the cut list's schema for a gesture that usually goes with looking.
calls.undo: Drop the pointing override in host-tin-owlet.ts, or key it on a new beat field.

calls.title: One pose per emotion loop, with a sign of the feeling (C1526)
options: One shared pose per emotion loop, effects drawn beside the bird, parts tucked in the still drawing
Keep the prototype's six poses by six expressions as a second choice under each emotion
Draw the wings hanging at the sides, changing the still drawing
calls.why: The emotion is already the one choice a beat makes, and the still drawing feeds the thumbnails, which should not change.
calls.undo: Edit an emotion's loop in host-tin-owlet.ts and re-pin its hash with a new contact sheet.

left: A change of emotion cuts from one loop to the next rather than blending the pose; only the box and opacity blend between beats today (#3564).
The pointing wing sits behind the body, so a point straight down shows only its tip below the belly.
Mochi's loops (HOST4) rebase onto host-draw.ts, the one helpers module, and fold their retouch helper into it.
